---
title: "After the course"
---
By the end of stage 5 you hold a case report, with a reproduction, an estimand statement and its causal graph, and a specification declared before it ran, and a project in a repository that another person can clone and re-render. The route took from each module of the [companion curriculum](../../companion/index.qmd) the sections that the case needed and left several out, and the list below gives the sections left out. Each module stands on its own, so take the one that your own work needs and leave the rest.

- [Reading the specification curve](../../companion/intro-r.qmd#sec-speccurve), the last section of the R module of this site, reads the curve of the case in R, aligned with the direction of the claim. The second part of Getting started with R, on the umbrella site, goes further with [the three dialects](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r-further.html#sec-dialects) in which R is written and [the habit of naming the estimand](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r-further.html#sec-estimand) before a model is read.
- [Multilevel models](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-multilevel), [Survey weights](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-weights), [Bayesian estimation](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-bayes) and [Bounded outcomes](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-glm) in the module on statistical methods take the other estimators of the course, among them survey weights in a panel of cells, the same model stated as a posterior, and an outcome bounded between 0 and 1.
- [A common scale](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-onescale) in the module on statistical methods, and [Cross-analyst comparisons](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd#sec-back) in the case study, put results from different estimators and outcome scales on one axis, the conversion behind the comparisons of Multi100.
- [Binary outcomes](../../companion/binary-outcomes.qmd) fits a single survey item as the outcome of a model, with clustered data, an interaction and a random intercept.
- [Graphs and data](../../companion/dags.qmd#sec-quartet) and [Your own graph](../../companion/dags.qmd#sec-yours) in the module on causal graphs say what no statistic computed from the data can settle about a causal graph, and draw a graph for a question of your own.
- [The items behind the scales](../../companion/measurement.qmd), [Weights](../../companion/weighting.qmd), [The individual level](../../companion/individual-level.qmd) and [Simulation as a method](../../companion/simulation.qmd), the optional readings of stage 4, take the measurement, the weights and the level of the analysis further.
- [The map](../../companion/data-sources.qmd#sec-map) and [Citing data](../../companion/data-sources.qmd#sec-citing) in the module on data sources say where else data for a question of your own are held, the access rule of each source, and how to cite a dataset, and [The macro indicators, at the World Bank](../../companion/data-sources.qmd#sec-worldbank) and [The published series](../../companion/data-sources.qmd#sec-series) take the macro series of the panel back to their sources.
- [The SCORE dossier on the OSF](../../companion/repositories.qmd#sec-score-dossiers), [The Multi100 records](../../companion/repositories.qmd#sec-multi100) and [The OSF after 2026](../../companion/repositories.qmd#sec-osf) in the module on repositories read the deposits of the case as records. The panel of the case is deposited in the OSF component maintained by its analyst, [osf.io/6zqct](https://osf.io/6zqct/).
- A replication of the claim on later Eurobarometer waves is not taught on this site. The data would be built from the files at GESIS by the route of stage 3, and [section 2.1 of the case study](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd#sec-repetition) reports the verdict of the SCORE replication on the waves of 2013 to 2019.

The formats with a facilitator suit anyone who wants to work through the case with others rather than alone: the one-day courses on its country-year panel, on [open science](../eu-frames-one-day-open-science/index.qmd), [data tools](../eu-frames-one-day-data-tools/index.qmd) and [methods](../eu-frames-one-day-methods/index.qmd), and the [three-day course](../eu-frames-three-days/index.qmd), which starts from the raw surveys and builds the analysis file of the case in class. The [AR4DS site](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/) describes the four cases of the course and holds its setup and help pages.
